newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower in sluggish trading on Monday, with sentiment poor and institutions sidelined following Changan Automobile's weak debut on Friday, analysts said.

The B share index shed 0.11 points, or 0.12 percent, to 88.80 on turnover of HK$15.50 million, compared with Friday's HK$27.40 million. But the A share index rose sharply in heavy trade, with heavy demand for Shenzhen-based property issues.
Analysts said B share market sentiment worsened after the poor debut on Friday of Changan, which closed sharply below its offer price of HK$1.89 per share.
Investor confidence has also been undermined by Shanghai B share market's repeatedly hitting record lows since last week, analysts said.
The market's medium-term performance will largely depend on listed firms' 1996 annual results, one broker said.
Nanshan Power Station was the worst performer with a loss of HK$0.24, or 10.71 percent, to HK$2.00 on volume of 400 shares early in the session.
Watch maker Fiyta followed, sliding HK$0.12, or 3.85 percent, to HK$3.00 after 22,400 shares were traded. Diesel engine manufacturer Changchai fell HK$0.18 to HK$4.70.

Changan rebounded on Monday due to bargain-hunting mainly by domestic institutions, brokers said. It rose HK$0.11, or 6.63 percent, to HK$1.77 in trading of 692,000 shares, making it the day's strongest performer. The issue's upward momentum does not appear strong because of the insufficient volume, brokers said.
China Marine, which fell sharply last week, held steady at HK$5.90, with 603,356 shares traded.
In contrast, the A share market gained sharply in heavy trade on Monday due in part to institutional demand for Shenzhen-based property issues, brokers said.
The A share index surged 16.54 points, or 4.37 percent, to 394.66, slightly off its intraday high of 394.76. Turnover rose to 11.39 billion yuan from 6.71 billion the previous session.
The composite index rose 14.85 points, or 4.22 percent, to 366.85.
Property issue Guiyang Zhongtian, the biggest gainer, soared 1.17 yuan, or 15.00 percent, to 8.97 yuan. Shenzhen Properties surged 1.03 yuan, or 11.98 percent, to 9.63 yuan.
